questions.question_text: A process that removes infection potentials by destroying microorganisms
questions.explanation: Sterilization is the complete destruction or removal of all forms of microorganisms.

questions.question_text: The holding temperature and minimum time using for moist heat sterilization in an autoclave
questions.explanation: Standard autoclave conditions for moist heat sterilization are typically $121^\circ\text{C}$ to $124^\circ\text{C}$ for 15-30 minutes under pressure.

questions.question_text: Which of the following filter is not a bacteria proof one ?
questions.explanation: Filter cloth has large pores and is used for coarse filtration, not retaining bacteria.

questions.question_text: Tablets which are designed to place under the tongue for disintegration/dissolution and absorption directly are called
questions.explanation: Sublingual tablets are placed under the tongue for rapid systemic absorption.

questions.question_text: Substances that reduce inter particular friction during compression of granules and friction between tablet and die wall during the ejection of tablets
questions.explanation: Lubricants decrease friction at the interface between the tablet's surface and the die wall during ejection.

questions.question_text: The property of an ideal enteric coating material, which is used for tablet coating is

options.D: Water proof coating is required prior to coating

questions.explanation: Enteric coating materials are designed to resist the acidic environment of the stomach and dissolve in the intestine.

questions.question_text: Cellulose acetate phthalate is a tablet coating material using for
questions.explanation: Cellulose acetate phthalate (CAP) is a well-known pH-sensitive polymer used for enteric coatings.

questions.question_text: Coacervation technique is used for
questions.explanation: Coacervation-phase separation is a primary chemical method used for microencapsulation.

questions.question_text: What is the use of Sorbitol in soft gelatin capsules ?
questions.explanation: Sorbitol is frequently used alongside glycerol as a plasticizer in soft gelatin capsule shells.

questions.question_text: The time specified for the disintegration of soft gelatin capsules as per Indian Pharmacopoeia
questions.explanation: According to the Indian Pharmacopoeia, soft gelatin capsules usually have a disintegration time limit of 60 minutes.

questions.question_text: Compound Tragacanth powder is using in suspension containing indiffusible solids as a
questions.explanation: Compound Tragacanth powder acts as a suspending agent and protective colloid to stabilize suspensions of indiffusible solids.

questions.question_text: The pharmaceutical substance light magnesium carbonate is a
questions.explanation: Light magnesium carbonate is classified as a diffusible solid in pharmacy compounding.

questions.question_text: What is the ratio of phenol and purified water for preparing liquefied phenol as per IP ?
questions.explanation: Liquefied phenol IP contains 80% w/w phenol, which corresponds to 80g of phenol and 20g of water (ratio 80 : 20).

questions.question_text: The Hydrophilic-Lipophilic-Balance (H.L.B.) range of o/w type emulsion forming emulgents is
questions.explanation: Emulsifying agents that form oil-in-water (o/w) emulsions generally have an HLB value ranging from 8 to 16, typically 13-15.

questions.question_text: In case of temporary or permanent renal failure, the removal of waste products and the maintenance of electrolyte balance, is done by
questions.explanation: Haemodialysis is the clinical process used to remove metabolic waste products and maintain electrolyte balance in renal failure.

questions.question_text: Cosmetic products which are used to reduce the sweat formation and body odour
questions.explanation: Antiperspirants reduce sweat formation, and deodorants mask or reduce body odor.

questions.question_text: Type of injections are given between the duramater and the inner aspects of the vertebra-route are
questions.explanation: Peridural (epidural) injections are administered into the epidural space, between the dura mater and the vertebral canal wall.

questions.question_text: The animal which is used to perform pyrogen test in injections
questions.explanation: Rabbits are traditionally used in the classic in vivo pyrogen test (USP/IP).

questions.question_text: Filter which is using for making the air in the aseptic area free from fibres, dust and microorganism
questions.explanation: HEPA (High Efficiency Particulate Air) filters are used to purify air in cleanrooms and aseptic areas.

questions.question_text: The base which is not suitable for the preparation of eye ointment base
questions.explanation: Yellow soft paraffin contains natural impurities and coloring matter, making white soft paraffin or purified bases preferred for ophthalmic use.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statement is correct about hydrochloric acid IP ?

options.A: It is an aqueous solution of hydrogen chloride in water and of purity not less than 35% w/w and not more than 38% w/w of HCl
options.B: It is an aqueous solution of hydrogen chloride in water and of purity not less than 38% w/w and not more than 40% w/w of HCl
options.C: It is a concentrated solution of hydrochloric acid of purity not less than 97% w/w and not more than 102% w/w of HCl
options.D: It is a concentrated solution of hydrochloric acid of purity not less than 95% w/w and not more than 100% w/w of HCl

questions.explanation: Concentrated hydrochloric acid IP contains about 35% to 38% w/w of HCl.

questions.question_text: Dilute hydrochloric should have purity and specific gravity _______ and _______ as per IP.

options.A: Purity 9.8 to 10.8% w/w and specific gravity 1.04 – 1.05 g/ml
options.B: Purity 8.5 to 10.5% w/w and specific gravity 1.34 – 1.15 g/ml
options.C: Purity 8.5 to 10.5% w/w and specific gravity 1.04 – 1.25 g/ml
options.D: Purity 9.5 to 10.5% w/w and specific gravity 1.04 – 1.05 g/ml

questions.explanation: Dilute hydrochloric acid IP contains 9.5% to 10.5% w/w HCl with a specific gravity of approximately 1.046 g/ml.

questions.question_text: Which one among the given options is not the natural source of boric acid ?
questions.explanation: Leucite is a potassium aluminum silicate mineral, not a borate source, whereas borocalcite, colemanite, and borax are natural borate minerals.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statement is correct about strong ammonium hydroxide solution ?

options.A: It is an aqueous solution of ammonia of purity not less than 27% w/v and not more than 30% w/v of ammonia
options.B: It is an aqueous solution of ammonia of purity not less than 37% w/v and not more than 42% w/v of ammonia
options.C: It is an aqueous solution of ammonia of purity not less than 32% w/v and not more than 38% w/v of ammonia
options.D: It is an aqueous solution of ammonia of purity not less than 27% w/v and not more than 32% w/v of ammonia

questions.explanation: Strong ammonium hydroxide solution contains 27% to 30% or up to 32% w/w depending on the pharmacopoeia, typically 27-32% w/v.

questions.question_text: Thiamine hydrochloride is sensitive to a pH over 5, hence thiamine hydrochloride injection B.P. is maintained at a pH
questions.explanation: Thiamine hydrochloride injection is maintained at an acidic pH of 3 to 4.5 to prevent degradation.

questions.question_text: Limit test for chlorides in potassium permanganate is performed by first decolorizing it by treating with
questions.explanation: Ethanol is commonly used to reduce and decolorize potassium permanganate in limit tests so that chloride impurities can be measured.

questions.question_text: Iodine tincture contains ___________ percentage of iodine.
questions.explanation: Weak iodine solution (iodine tincture) typically contains 2.5% w/v of iodine.

questions.question_text: Borax is
questions.explanation: Borax chemically is sodium tetraborate decahydrate (disodium tetraborate).

questions.question_text: Twenty volume hydrogen peroxide aqueous solution should contain not less than ____________ $H_2O_2$.
questions.explanation: A 20-volume hydrogen peroxide solution releases 20 times its volume of oxygen, corresponding to approximately 6% w/v $H_2O_2$.

questions.question_text: Which statement is/are true about ammonium chloride? i) Ammonium chloride is assayed by Volhard's method. ii) Ammonium chloride is assayed by acid-base titration. iii) Ammonium chloride is a reflux expectorant. iv) Ammonium chloride is an antidote for cyanide poisoning.
questions.explanation: Ammonium chloride is assayed by acid-base titration (back titration), used as an expectorant, and can be assayed via methods including modified approaches, while cyanide uses specific antidotes like sodium nitrite.

questions.question_text: Proflavine is an acridine derivative having two amino groups at positions
questions.explanation: Proflavine is 3,6-diaminoacridine.

questions.question_text: ___________ is a long-acting sulphonamide.
questions.explanation: Sulphadimethoxine is classified as a long-acting sulfonamide.

questions.question_text: ___________ is an antibiotic having hydronaphthalene ring.
questions.explanation: Tetracyclines possess a characteristic octahydrotetracene-carboxamide (hydronaphthalene-based) ring system.

questions.question_text: Beta-lactum ring is having double bond between __________ which maintains the strained ring system and increases beta-lactamase resistance.
questions.explanation: In certain modified beta-lactams or related fused rings, unsaturation positions contribute to stability and resistance profiles.

questions.question_text: Which antimalarial drug given below is a fully substituted pyrimidine?
questions.explanation: Pyrimethamine is a diaminopyrimidine derivative acting as a dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor.

questions.question_text: Chlorpromazine has the following biological actions except __________ action. Select the exception from the options.
questions.explanation: Chlorpromazine is a typical antipsychotic with sedative, anti-emetic, and antipruritic properties, but it is not used as an anticancer drug.

questions.question_text: The drug which is not a catecholamine is
questions.explanation: Ephedrine lacks the catechol (3,4-dihydroxyphenyl) nucleus, unlike adrenaline, noradrenaline, and dopamine.

questions.question_text: Atropine has the following uses except ___________. Select the exception from the options.

options.C: Used as Antispasmodic in radiological examination of gut
options.D: Used to treat urinary tract obstruction

questions.explanation: Atropine causes urinary retention, so it is not used to treat urinary tract obstruction.

questions.question_text: ___________ is a loop diuretic.
questions.explanation: Furosemide is a high-ceiling loop diuretic acting on the ascending limb of the loop of Henle.

questions.question_text: __________ is the anticancer drug which acts as antimetabolite of folic acid.
questions.explanation: Methotrexate is a well-known antifolate drug used in cancer chemotherapy.

questions.question_text: Aloe emodin present in aloe is detected by
questions.explanation: Modified Borntrager's test is used to detect C-glyycosides and emodins present in drugs like Aloe.

questions.question_text: The aroma of ginger is due to the presence of
questions.explanation: Zingiberene is the primary sesquiterpene responsible for the characteristic aroma/odor of ginger.

questions.question_text: Vanillin is synthesized from
questions.explanation: Commercial synthesis of vanillin is frequently achieved using eugenol as a starting material.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drug is used as cardiac depressant?
questions.explanation: Cinchona alkaloids like quinidine act as cardiac depressants (antiarrhythmics).

questions.question_text: Which crude drug is known as St. Antony's fire?
questions.explanation: Ergotism, caused by ergot alkaloids, was historically known as St. Anthony's fire.

questions.question_text: The saponin glycoside present in digitalis is
questions.explanation: Digitonin is a well-known saponin glycoside found in Digitalis purpurea.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the source of citral?
questions.explanation: Lemongrass oil is a rich natural source of the aldehyde citral.

questions.question_text: Paracytic stomata is present in
questions.explanation: Senna leaves characteristically exhibit paracytic (rubiaceous) stomata.

questions.question_text: The euginol content of clove oil is
questions.explanation: Clove oil typically contains between 85% to 90% eugenol.

questions.question_text: Papain is used as
questions.explanation: Papain is a proteolytic enzyme used principally for its anti-inflammatory and digestive properties.

questions.question_text: Which among the following is not an atypical antipsychotic agent?
questions.explanation: Bupropion is an antidepressant (NDRI), whereas risperidone, olanzapine, and zotepine are atypical antipsychotics.

questions.question_text: ___________ is a vasicoselective anticholinergic agent.
questions.explanation: Flavoxate is a urinary antispasmodic known for its selective action on the urinary bladder (vasicoselective).

questions.question_text: Compound used in the treatment of morphine addiction is
questions.explanation: Methadone is a long-acting synthetic opioid used in substitution therapy for opioid/morphine addiction.

questions.question_text: Antihypertensive agent safely used in pregnancy
questions.explanation: Methyldopa is a standard, safe choice for treating hypertension during pregnancy.

questions.question_text: Drug effective in petitmal epilepsy
questions.explanation: Ethosuximide is the drug of choice for absence (petit mal) seizures.

questions.question_text: A protease inhibitor used in the treatment of AIDS
questions.explanation: Indinavir is an antiretroviral drug of the protease inhibitor class.

questions.question_text: Which among the following is a source of nitric oxide?
questions.explanation: Glyceryl trinitrate (nitroglycerin) is a classic nitric oxide donor used for angina.

questions.question_text: Malignant hyperthermia is associated with which among the following drug?
questions.explanation: Halothane, along with succinylcholine, can trigger malignant hyperthermia in susceptible individuals.

questions.question_text: Which among the following is an example for drug synergism?
questions.explanation: Cotrimoxazole (sulfamethoxazole + trimethoprim) demonstrates potentiation/synergism in antibacterial action.

questions.question_text: Urinary infection is common with which among the following antidiabetic agent?
questions.explanation: SGLT2 inhibitors like canagliflozin promote glucosuria, which increases the incidence of urinary tract infections.

questions.question_text: The date in which the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act and Rules, 1985 came into force in India on
questions.explanation: The NDPS Act came into force on November 14, 1985.

questions.question_text: According to Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985, poppy straw is defined as

options.A: All parts of the opium poppy after harvesting
options.B: All parts (except the seeds) of the opium poppy after harvesting whether in their original form
options.C: All parts (except the leaves and stem) after harvesting of the plant opium poppy
options.D: Juice from the seeds and leaves of opium poppy after harvesting

questions.explanation: Poppy straw is legally defined under the NDPS Act as all parts (except the seeds) of the opium poppy after harvesting whether in their original form or cut, crushed, or powdered.

questions.question_text: The minimum number of registered pharmacist normally nominated by the state government to the state pharmacy council
questions.explanation: Under the Pharmacy Act, the state government nominates 5 members, of whom at least 3 must be registered pharmacists.

questions.question_text: The trial for the offences under Drugs and Magic Remedies Act and Rules, 1955 can be carried out only in
questions.explanation: Offences under the Drugs and Magic Remedies Act are tried by a Presidency Magistrate or a Magistrate of the first class.

questions.question_text: The punishment for a subsequent violation of Drugs and Magic Remedies Act and Rules, 1955 is

options.A: Imprisonment upto 3 months or with fine or both
options.B: Imprisonment upto 6 months or with fine or both
options.C: Imprisonment upto 12 months or with fine or both
options.D: Imprisonment upto 24 months or with fine or both

questions.explanation: Subsequent conviction under the Drugs and Magic Remedies Act carries imprisonment up to 6 months, with fine, or both.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statement is correct about spurious drugs?

options.A: Drugs not labelled in the prescribed manner
options.B: Drugs which bear names of other drugs
options.C: Drugs containing color other than those prescribed
options.D: Drugs packed in containers composed of poisonous or deleterious substance

questions.explanation: A drug is deemed spurious if it is imported under a name of another drug or mimics another drug deceptively.

questions.question_text: The license for retail sale of Schedule X drugs is issued in
questions.explanation: Form 20F is prescribed for the issue of a license to sell, stock, or exhibit for sale Schedule X drugs by retail.

questions.question_text: The sample taken by a drugs inspector from a drug manufacturing premise is divided into
questions.explanation: Under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act rules, samples taken for test or analysis are typically divided into 4 portions.

questions.question_text: Which among the given drugs belong to Schedule C1 class?
questions.explanation: Insulin injection is listed under Schedule C1 biological and special products.

questions.question_text: As per Schedule P of the Drugs and Cosmetic Act and Rules 1945, store in a cool place refers to the temperature
questions.explanation: Schedule P defines 'cool place' as a temperature between 8°C and 15°C.

questions.question_text: The minimum desirable area to open a combined wholesale and retail drug store is
questions.explanation: A combined wholesale and retail pharmacy requires a minimum area of 20 square meters.

questions.question_text: In the combination codification system to arrange the items in a pharmacy drug store, which codes are combined together?
questions.explanation: Combination codification systems typically integrate alphabetical and numerical methods.

questions.question_text: For materials like menthol, which are subject to wastage during storage, the pricing method commonly used
questions.explanation: Materials subject to loss or shrinkage during storage (like sublimation in menthol) are often priced using an inflated price method to cover the wastage.

questions.question_text: The perpetual inventory system comprises of

options.A: Bin card, stores ledger and periodic report
options.B: Bin card, periodic report and moving ratios
options.C: Bin card, stores ledger and continuous stock taking
options.D: Bin card, moving ratios and vital items

questions.explanation: A perpetual inventory system relies on bin cards, stores ledgers, and continuous stock taking to maintain real-time inventory control.

questions.question_text: The equation used for calculating maximum stock level is

options.A: Re-order quantity – Re-order level + Minimum consumption
options.B: Re-order quantity + Re-order level – Maximum consumption
options.C: Re-order quantity + Re-order level – Minimum consumption
options.D: Re-order quantity × Re-order level – Maximum consumption

questions.explanation: Maximum stock level = Re-order level + Re-order quantity - (Minimum consumption $\times$ Minimum lead time), simplified as Re-order quantity + Re-order level - Minimum consumption.

questions.question_text: Which among the following is a social quality needed for a salesman?
questions.explanation: Being polite and courteous represents an essential social quality for customer interaction.

questions.question_text: Which is the main method used for advertising ethical pharmaceutical products?
questions.explanation: Detailing (personal selling to physicians by medical representatives) is the primary method for promoting ethical prescription drugs.

questions.question_text: Which bank is mainly promoting export-import business in India ?
questions.explanation: The Export-Import Bank of India (EXIM Bank) is the premier export finance institution in the country.

questions.question_text: The working capital required by a business is normally not used for
questions.explanation: Working capital is used for short-term operational expenses, whereas the purchase of machinery is a capital expenditure.

questions.question_text: Which application form (as per Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945) is used to apply for a retail drug store license ?
questions.explanation: Form 20 is the application form for a license to sell, stock, or exhibit for sale drugs other than those specified in Schedule C, C(1) and X (retail drug store license).

questions.question_text: Name the instrument used to fix surgical towels in place during surgery.
questions.explanation: Horsley's type clip and towel clips are commonly used to secure surgical drapes and towels.

questions.question_text: Which is the health accessory used by the patient to promote proper body alignment ?
questions.explanation: Orthopaedic braces are designed to support and align body parts correctly.

questions.question_text: The first scientific Hospital Formulary in India was published in which year ?
questions.explanation: The first hospital formulary in India was published in 1968 by the昌 All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS).

questions.question_text: Which of the statement is true for Beta propiolactone as an non-inflammable liquid to sterilize things in CSSD ?
questions.explanation: Beta-propiolactone is a sterilizing agent that is a known irritant, can cause respiratory issues, and is a suspected carcinogen.

questions.question_text: What is the use of diffuser in a sterile manufacturing area in a hospital ?

options.A: Used to throw the particles towards the corner
options.D: To increase the visibility of manufacturing unit

questions.explanation: Diffusers help regulate airflow and maintain environmental control in cleanrooms.

questions.question_text: Name the test which is employed to find out leakage in thermolabile products in hospital manufacturing.
questions.explanation: The spark detector method or high-voltage test is used to detect pinholes and cracks in ampoules without thermal stress.

questions.question_text: Which one is the computer based database used to predict Pharmacokinetic parameters in a hospital set up ?
questions.explanation: MEDIPHOR is a well-known computer-based monitoring system used in hospital pharmacy for drug data and pharmacokinetics.

questions.question_text: What are the components present in the IV set, except ?
questions.explanation: An IV set includes a plastic spike, drip chamber, and flow regulator, while the IV admixture is the fluid/drug mixture added to the system.

questions.question_text: Dissertations are comes under which type of source of information ?
questions.explanation: Dissertations and theses contain original research data, classifying them as primary sources.

questions.question_text: “Mobile dispensing unit” is mainly adopted to give medicines to patients comes under which type of drug distribution system ?
questions.explanation: Mobile dispensing units are frequently utilized in unit dose drug distribution systems within hospitals.

questions.question_text: Which drug causes the ADR cleft palate ?
questions.explanation: Phenytoin is well known to cause fetal hydantoin syndrome, which frequently includes cleft lip and palate.

questions.question_text: “Cheese reaction” is an example of which type of interaction ?
questions.explanation: The cheese reaction occurs due to the interaction between MAOIs and tyramine-rich foods like aged cheese.

questions.question_text: The interaction of barbiturates and MAOIs causes
questions.explanation: MAOIs inhibit the metabolism of barbiturates, leading to prolonged central nervous system depression.

questions.question_text: Which is used as an antidote for acute iron toxicity ?
questions.explanation: Desferrioxamine is a specific chelating agent used as an antidote for iron poisoning.

questions.question_text: Name the method used to stimulate respiration in a poisoned person.
questions.explanation: Anal stretch (known as Laborde or other historical resuscitation techniques) was historically cited in toxicology texts to stimulate respiration.

questions.question_text: Which chemical agent can be used for alkalinisation of urine in barbiturate poisoning ?
questions.explanation: Sodium bicarbonate is administered intravenously to alkalinize the urine, enhancing the renal elimination of weak acids like barbiturates.

questions.question_text: As a Clinical Pharmacist, what drug would you recommend to relieve morning sickness in first trimester of pregnancy ?
questions.explanation: Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) is widely recommended and safe for treating nausea and vomiting in pregnancy.

questions.question_text: “Gooseflesh” is one of the withdrawal symptoms of which type of drug use ?
questions.explanation: Piloerection, commonly known as 'gooseflesh', is a classic withdrawal symptom of opioid/narcotic dependence.

questions.question_text: Name the condition which explains “is a state of periodic or chronic intoxication produced by the repeated consumption of a drug”.
questions.explanation: Drug addiction is defined by WHO as a state of periodic or chronic intoxication produced by the repeated consumption of a drug.

questions.question_text: Azoturia is a clinical manifestation for the disease
questions.explanation: Azoturia (excess nitrogen compounds in urine) can be seen in metabolic conditions like severe diabetes mellitus involving protein catabolism.
